name: Philetas of Samos
bio: Philetas of Samos is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 481).

poems.title: Book VII, 481
poems.author: Philetas of Samos
poems.text: The grave-stone heavy with grief says “Death has carried away short-lived little Theodota,” and the little one says again to her father, “Theodotus, cease to grieve; mortals are often unfortunate.”

poems.title: The Closed Account (Mackail)
poems.author: Philetas of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: I weep not for thee, O dearest of friends; for thou knewest many fair things; and again God dealt thee thy lot of ill.

poems.title: Anthologia Graeca VII.481: Οὐ κλαίω, ξείνων σε φιλαίτατε
poems.author: Philetas of Samos
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology, Greek text (Mackail, 1890)
poems.text:
Οὐ κλαίω, ξείνων σε φιλαίτατε· πολλὰ γὰρ ἔγνως
καλά· κακῶν δ᾽ αὖ σοὶ μοῖραν ἔνειμε θεός.
